title: Glossary.
caption: The terms this paper uses, the names they carry in the code, and, where it differs, the meaning in OpenZeppelin's account or in oz-policy-builder. The vision companion paper has the full glossary.
rows: A bounded set of rules the owner installs so an app can act without a prompt for each call
No single object: one context rule per contract, each with its policies
The JSON a wallet submits to install a grant; an input and a hash commitment
The rules and metadata stored under a grant ID, stamped with the grant generation
One target contract, function list, argument conditions and signer threshold, with optional expiry, cap and generation
The contract whose functions a rule lets be called
Which listed signers must approve: a threshold over distinct identities
The rule's signers, with a threshold policy attached
Key material plus a verifier contract that checks evidence for it (Ed25519, WebAuthn passkey)
Same enum case; refused on rules the interpreter polices (error {{fact:opb-error-external-signer}})
Another Soroban address that approves through the host; in Perch through CAP-0071, inside the account's own authorization entry
Same enum case; approves in an authorization entry of its own, binding the rule IDs; the only kind on policed rules
A contract with `verify(digest, key, signature) -> bool`
The same interface for External signers
A stateless contract that parses and validates a document, resolves verifier names and returns canonical bytes, `doc_hash` and a model
The pure function that decides an authorization and returns the next spending records
The account code around the decision function: guards, rule lookup, signature checks and storage; tested, not proved
Turning a compiled document's model into the rules the account stores, under the account's address, its excluded set and the current grant generation
A capped rule's charged amounts and their ledgers
The smallest unit of XLM: {{fact:stroops-per-xlm}} stroops make one XLM
At most *limit* charged over the last *P* ledgers: the window at ledger *L* is (*L* − *P*, *L*]
`spending_limit` uses the same window boundary. In an oz-policy-builder Intent, `cap` bounds one call (`lte`)
Deriving from a grant a rule set that allows nothing the original does not, by the ten steps of rule-core's attenuation; modeled and proved, with no account entry point at the pinned build
A counter on the account, 0 at creation, advanced only by a completed recovery; a grant from an older generation refuses
One call or contract creation in the invocation tree the host passes to `__check_auth`
The same; a context rule matches it
Signed credentials for one invocation tree; the host consumes its nonce when the transaction succeeds
The account function the host calls to approve an authorization entry; it receives the payload hash, the auth payload and the contexts
The argument of `__check_auth` whose shape the account defines: the signatures and the rule chosen for each context
A simulation that runs `__check_auth`, so it predicts a refusal; recording simulation, which discovers which entries a transaction needs, does not
OpenZeppelin's unit of authorization: a context type, signers, policies and an optional `valid_until`
A contract attached to a context rule; the account calls its `enforce` after authenticating (hooks `install`, `uninstall`, `enforce`)
The expression the interpreter stores per (account, rule) and evaluates in `enforce`

No counterpart: Perch decides in the account. The policy contract of Perch's earlier design ({{fact:perch-deployed-account-version}}) is still pinned by the account and never called (the vision paper)
The account's owner-authorized call as the account
The adapter's batch call `execute(calls, grants, wait)`
The library that holds the evaluator, its Lean model, the translation and the proofs
The proof assistant whose kernel checks the theorems
